nodes.summary: For a list $C = (g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$ of serialized gates and a list $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of Booleans, the gate values of $C$ on $a$ are the list of gate values of the flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs whose $j$-th gate is decoded from the (kind, references) pair $g_j$, evaluated on the assignment that gives input $i$ the value $a_i$.
nodes.title: Gate values of a serialized circuit

nodes.summary: For a list $C$ of serialized gates, a list $a$ of Booleans and a natural number $k$, the outputs of $C$ on $a$ are the last $k$ entries of the gate values of $C$ on $a$, or all of them when $C$ has fewer than $k$ gates.
nodes.title: Outputs of a serialized circuit

nodes.summary: For $n$-bit strings $y$ and $r$, their concatenation is the $2n$-bit string whose bit $i$ is $y_i$ for $i < n$ and $r_{i - n}$ for $n \le i < 2n$.
nodes.title: Concatenation of two bitstrings

nodes.summary: A serialized gate is a pair $(k, r)$ of a natural number $k$, the kind of the gate, and a list $r$ of natural numbers, its references.
nodes.title: Serialized circuit gates

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a family of bijections $\pi_n$ of the set of $n$-bit strings, one for each natural number $n$. Suppose that $\pi$ is computable by polynomial-size circuits: there is a polynomial $q$ with natural number coefficients such that for every $n$ some list of at most $q(n)$ serialized gates has, on every $n$-bit string $x$, outputs (its last $n$ gate values) equal to $\pi_n(x)$. Suppose also that $\pi$ is…
nodes.title: Goldreich-Levin: hardcore predicate from one-way permutations

nodes.summary: For a list $C$ of serialized gates and a map $\pi$ from $n$-bit strings to $n$-bit strings, the inversion success probability of $C$ against $\pi$ is the rational number $N / 2^n$, where $N$ is the number of $n$-bit strings $x$ such that the outputs of $C$ on input $\pi(x)$, taken as its last $n$ gate values, are exactly $x$.
nodes.title: Inversion success probability of a circuit

nodes.summary: For a list $C$ of serialized gates and a map $\pi$ from $n$-bit strings to $n$-bit strings, the prediction success probability of $C$ against $\pi$ is the rational number $N / 2^{2n}$, where $N$ is the number of pairs $(x, r)$ of $n$-bit strings such that $C$ has at least one gate and the value of its last gate on the concatenation of $\pi(x)$ and $r$, a $2n$-bit input, equals the inner product of $x$ and $r$…
nodes.title: Prediction success probability for the inner-product bit

nodes.summary: For $n$-bit strings $x$ and $r$, their inner product modulo 2 is true if and only if the number of indices $i < n$ with $x_i$ and $r_i$ both true is odd, that is, $\langle x, r \rangle = \sum_{i < n} x_i r_i \bmod 2$.
nodes.title: Inner product modulo 2

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
